subject: Medix VPC deployment — audit windows, operator access, and MSA redlines
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medixhealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VPC deployment — audit window and operator access (Medix)

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the intake call yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a written list of audit and deployment asks tied to the MSA/order form for our VPC-hosted deployment. The high-level items are: 

- Clarify whether Redwood will allow temporary audited access (witnessing) to a forensic snapshot in the event of a termination-triggered handback.
- Define the operator-access boundary: who at Redwood can access our VPC instance and under what controls.
- Audit window length and notice requirements for a scheduled audit (we typically request 30 days).
- Evidence items for procurement (SOC2, KMS attestation, snapshot provenance).

I've attached a spreadsheet with our standard fields (Medix_VPC_Audit_Requests.xlsx). Can you confirm Redwood's baseline position so we can start redlining the MSA and the order form? Procurement would like to schedule a short call next week to align legal + infra.

Appreciate it —
Sara
Sara Liu
Senior Procurement Manager | Medix Health
attachments: Medix_VPC_Audit_Requests.xlsx

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medixhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC deployment — audit window and operator access (Medix)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. 

Quick baseline from Redwood: 
- We can support temporary, customer-initiated snapshot review for on-prem / private installs. For VPC we typically offer a "witness-lite" pathway that avoids full operator presence by delivering a cryptographic snapshot (SHA256 manifest) plus time-stamped transfer logs.
- Operator access to customer-owned VPCs is restricted to named ops engineers and only under documented runbook steps; escalation requires a documented change request and approval from the customer security contact.
- We are generally OK with a 30-day audit notice window; we prefer a 14–30 day configurable notice depending on the scope.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and KMS attestation excerpts; certain forensic artifacts (full VM images) are treated as high-sensitivity and governed by exhibit terms.

I've looped in our legal (Laura) and contracts lead (Jordan) to propose specific MSA/order form language. I'll attach a short set of proposed redline notes for the order form to get the conversation started. Can we schedule procurement + legal sync next Wed (21 Feb) at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
attachments: Proposed_MSA_Redlines_ConnorsNotes.docx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: VPC deployment — proposed language for MSA/order form addendum

Connor — forwarding my suggested text for the MSA addendum. Below are the high-level edits I propose (I put full redline in the attached doc):

1) Replacement of a mandatory "on-site witnessing" requirement with an option for a "cryptographic snapshot deposit" plus certified transfer logs. Suggested clause: 
"In lieu of physical witnessing, Customer and Provider may elect a cryptographic snapshot deposit process: Provider will produce a time-stamped, signed snapshot hash and associated transfer manifest; Customer may require Provider to make available a dedicated read-only forensic artifact under mutually agreed secure transfer procedures."

2) Operator access: limit to named Provider personnel and require customer security approval + pre-authorized runbook for emergency access. Add explicit recordkeeping obligations (audit logs retained for at least 365 days).

3) Audit window: propose 30 calendar days' notice for full-scope audits; 14 days for targeted/limited audits. Add mutual cooperation clause for scheduling.

4) Evidence: SOC2 Type II + KMS attestation to be listed as acceptable baseline deliverables. For higher-sensitivity requests we can commit to a documented exhibit and additional fees.

I am attaching the redline for the MSA/order form addendum: MSA_Orderform_Addendum_redline_20280214.docx. Jordan: please flag any commercial risk on operator access carveouts or fee items that should land in the order form.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_Orderform_Addendum_redline_20280214.docx

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medixhealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com, ben.thornton@gridcloud.com
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2028 10:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC deployment — audit window and operator access (Medix)

Connor/Laura/Jordan — thanks for the draft language; procurement has a few clarifying items before we loop legal: 

- For the snapshot deposit approach: who performs the snapshot? Medix IT prefers that a mutually agreed third party or an on-site customer engineer performs the capture; is Redwood able to support an escorted capture or supply instructions and a signed manifest?
- Our procurement team needs confirmation that the cryptographic manifest will be anchored to a provider KMS key (or HSM) and that we will receive the related attestation.
- Procurement also asked about limits on frequency (e.g., how often can we request a snapshot in a 12‑month period) and potential fee schedule for snapshot delivery.

I've attached our procurement SLA and evidence checklist for reference (Procurement_SLA_Sheet.pdf). Can you call out the attachment points for the order form (exhibit numbers) in your next redline so procurement can map to our internal purchasing controls?

If you can confirm these points before our call, it will speed legal review.

Best,
Sara
attachments: Procurement_SLA_Sheet.pdf

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medixhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Mar 2028 15:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC deployment — audit window and operator access (Medix)

Hi Sara — quick consolidated reply after internal legal/infra sync. Apologies for the lag — want to make sure we give procurement concrete touchpoints.

1) Snapshot capture: two supported pathways
   - Customer-directed capture: Medix performs the capture using Provider-supplied capture instructions; Provider validates the manifest and returns a signed hash (no Provider write access required).
   - Provider-assisted capture: Redwood assists under escrow-like controls (escrow engineer present via secure session) for a limited fee; access limited to named personnel with pre-authorized runbook.

2) Manifest attestation: We will anchor the manifest signature to a Redwood KMS key and provide a signed attestation (HSM-backed). We can include the attestation as part of Exhibit B (forensic access & evidence) in the order form addendum.

3) Frequency/fees: Baseline includes one complimentary snapshot on contract start and one per 12 months; additional requests are billable per the Order Form fee schedule (we'll map explicit pricing in a separate Order Form exhibit).

4) Exhibit mapping: we'll propose Exhibit B = Forensic Access & Snapshot Process; Exhibit C = Operator Access & Runbook; Exhibit D = Evidence & Compliance Deliverables (SOC2/KMS attestations). I'll update the redline to include these exhibit references and re-share via DocuSign.

Next steps:
- I'll attach the updated redline and proposed exhibit placeholders to the DocuSign room (link below).
- Let's keep the scheduled procurement call on 21 Feb if that still works — if not, propose an alternate.
